name: Z-Guard Sweeps & Deep Half
keyCorrections: If you can't slide into deep half, your underhook is not deep enough — drive your shoulder further under their armpit.
If the waiter sweep doesn't work, their weight is too far back — switch to wrestle-up.
If they flatten you, you lost the underhook — pummel back to it before trying to sweep.
description: Use the knee shield (Z-guard) and underhook to create deep half entries, waiter sweeps, or wrestle-up opportunities from the bottom half guard.
shortInstruction: Knee shield, underhook, feel their weight — slide into deep half or sweep from Z-guard.
summary: Z-guard (knee shield) is the control position; sweeps are the payoff. From Z-guard, your knee shield creates distance while you fight for the underhook. Once you win the underhook, you have three main sweep options: slide into deep half (when they drive forward), hit the waiter sweep (when they stand), or wrestle up (when they back away). The Z-guard to deep half transition is one of the highest percentage sweep chains in no-gi.
whyItWorks: The knee shield prevents chest pressure, giving you time to find the underhook.
Winning the underhook gives you the control point to enter deep half — without it, deep half is impossible.
Your bottom half guard sweeps exploit their forward momentum — the harder they drive, the easier the sweep.
Danaher principle: half guard sweeps are not about strength — they are about weight timing and angle.
commonMistakes: Trying to sweep without winning the underhook first — the underhook is the key to all half guard sweeps.
Going to deep half when they are postured up — deep half works when they drive forward, not when they stand.
Using only your arms to sweep — the power comes from your hip movement and leg drive.
Staying in Z-guard too long — Z-guard is control; sweeps are the exit.
coachingCues: Win the underhook, then sweep — never before.
Feel their weight — forward is deep half, back is wrestle-up.
Slide your hips under theirs, not next to them.
Z-guard is the waiting room — sweeps are the exit door.
safetySummary: Do not crank your partner's neck during underhook battles — keep your head in their chest, not their neck.
When entering deep half, protect your face from their crossfacing arm.
If they stack you during the sweep, bail out and reset — do not let them drive your head into the mat.

systemLogic.corePrinciple: Z-guard (knee shield) → win underhook → read their weight → choose sweep.

decisionTree.action: slide into deep half → waiter sweep or back take.

moneyDetails: The underhook must be deep — your shoulder should be under their armpit, not just your arm wrapped around their back.
To enter deep half, slide your head to the far side of their body while keeping the underhook.
The waiter sweep works by pushing their far knee with your foot while pulling their near leg — scissor motion.
If they resist the sweep by stepping back, follow them and enter single-leg X.
nextStep: After Z-guard sweeps, learn the deep half guard and waiter sweep in detail.
fixItFast: Can't slide into deep half? Your underhook is too shallow — dig deeper under their armpit.
They keep backing out? Stop chasing — wrestle up instead.
Waiter sweep not working? Push their far knee, not their hip — the knee is the tipping point.
